classification.difficultyReason: Select the congruent pair from three triangles, distinguish sufficient markings from distractors, and order corresponding vertices.

content.prompt: For each set of three triangles, choose the two that are congruent. Choose the appropriate test (SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS) and write a congruence statement (e.g. $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta FGH$).

spec.description: Three separate triangles in source order ABC, DEF, UTS, with outward vertex labels. Ordinary source-blue geometry is reconstructed in black.
spec.mathematics: Right angles at B, E and T. BC and UT have one tick; AC, DF and US have two ticks. DEF has no marked leg.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens appear; no congruence statement or test is printed.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC=\angle STU=90^\circ$, $AC=SU$ and $BC=TU$. The hypotenuse and one corresponding side are equal, so $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta STU$ by RHS.

spec.description: Three triangles arranged left to right as ABC, DEF and GHI; all source tick counts retained and ordinary geometry black.
spec.mathematics: AB, DE and GH have one tick. BC, EF and HI have two ticks. DF and GI have three ticks. CA is unmarked.
spec.answerVisibility: Student figure contains no supplied answer.

answer.worked: $DE=GH$, $EF=HI$ and $DF=GI$. Three pairs of corresponding sides are equal, so $\Delta DEF\equiv\Delta GHI$ by SSS.

spec.description: Three triangles in source order; filled dots retain their meaning as corresponding-angle markers rather than labelled interior points.
spec.mathematics: AB, ED and IG have one tick; BC, EF and IH have two ticks. Equal-angle dots occur at B, E and H. Only B and E are included between the marked sides.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or additional angle mark is supplied.

answer.worked: $AB=DE$, $BC=EF$ and $\angle ABC=\angle DEF$. Two corresponding sides and their included angle are equal, so $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta DEF$ by SAS.

spec.description: Three triangles in source order with two distinct corresponding-angle marker classes: crosses and filled dots.
spec.mathematics: Crosses at A, D and G; dots at B, E and H. Single ticks on BC, ED and HI. ED lies between the two marked angles; BC and HI correspond and do not lie between the marked angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original givens are shown.

answer.worked: $\angle BAC=\angle HGI$, $\angle ABC=\angle GHI$ and $BC=HI$. Two corresponding angles and one corresponding side are equal, so $\Delta ABC\equiv\Delta GHI$ by AAS.
